div.div:
Credentials
Each login's password is a Kubernetes Secret rendered by External Secrets from OpenBao KV and reloaded by CNPG: secret/local/databases/<cluster>/<service>-runtime and -migrator for services on the RFC-0029 roles (every platform-db service, product and inventory on product-db), <cluster>/<service> for the rest. notification_runtime is the exception: its password is owned by the OpenBao database engine, which rotates it every 720 h, and External Secrets reads database/static-creds/notification-runtime every minute. PgDog takes the product-db role secrets through its HelmRelease valuesFrom; backups authenticate to RustFS with pg-backup-rustfs-credentials.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1508px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1085px; margin-left: 12px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #475569;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#475569, #9ba7b8); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Why the DR replica reads from RustFS
product-db-replica never connects to the primary: it bootstraps from product-db's base backup and then replays its WAL archive from the bucket, so it survives the loss of the product-db pods. Its designated primary keeps its own archive and a daily backup in product-db-replica/ (7 d). Migrations always target the -rw service directly, never a pooler.
